subject: Cloud Computing
title: Monitoring and Observability
description: A short lesson to help you apply Monitoring and Observability.

hook.text: Your app is slow but you don't know why. Without monitoring, the cloud is a black box.

buildup.text: Monitoring tracks metrics: CPU, memory, error rates, response times. It tells you what's happening.

discovery.text: Observability goes deeper: logs, traces, and metrics together explain why something went wrong.

twist.text: Cloud systems generate so much telemetry that finding the signal in the noise is its own challenge.

climax.text: Tools like CloudWatch, Datadog, and Grafana turn raw data into dashboards that humans can understand.

punchline.text: You can't fix what you can't see. Monitoring is sight.

quiz.question: What is the difference between monitoring and observability?
options: Monitoring shows what's happening; observability explains why
Monitoring is for hardware; observability is for software
They are exactly the same concept with different names

details.summary: Cloud monitoring collects metrics, logs, and traces from infrastructure and applications to provide visibility into system health and performance. Observability tools like CloudWatch, Stackdriver, and Azure Monitor enable alerting on anomalies and diagnosing issues before users are affected.
details.whyItMatters: You cannot manage what you cannot measure. Cloud monitoring and observability are essential for maintaining reliability, optimizing performance, and controlling costs in complex distributed systems.
takeaways: Metrics, logs, and traces form the three pillars of observability
Automated alerts detect problems before users report them
Cloud-native monitoring integrates with all provider services

faq.question: What is the difference between monitoring and observability?
faq.answer: Monitoring tracks known metrics and alerts on predefined thresholds. Observability enables exploring unknown problems by correlating metrics, logs, and traces. Monitoring tells you when something breaks; observability helps you understand why it broke.

faq.question: What should be monitored in a cloud environment?
faq.answer: Monitor infrastructure metrics like CPU and memory, application metrics like response time and error rates, business metrics like transactions and user sessions, and cost metrics like spending trends. Set alerts for anomalies in each category.
